The product team pitches the terminal surface as determinism for AI-assisted development. By Steef-Jan Wig

title: Google Open-Sources TPU Sync for KV Cache and Weight Transfer on TPUs
summary: Google Cloud has open-sourced TPU Sync, a native C++ library that moves KV cache blocks and model weights between TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network. By Daniel Dominguez

title: Author Q+A: finprim is a Case for One Financial Validation Library in TypeScript
summary: finprim is an MIT-licensed TypeScript library that offers IBAN, BIC, card, sort code, VAT, routing number and loan functions through one API with no runtime dependencies. Its author built it after duplicated validators drifted apart across web and mobile. It validates and formats data only, and does not process payments. He is cautious about adding SEPA and ACH file generation. By Daniel Curtis

title: LinkedIn Replaces Argo CD with a Custom GitOps Engine for Kubernetes Deployments

title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows Generally Available with Isolation and Budget Controls

title: JioHotstar Benchmarks Knowledge Bases for AI Coding Agents
summary: JioHotstar evaluated 6 approaches to code retrieval for AI coding agents using SWE, CodeScale Bench, and an internal question-answering harness. Structural search performed well on concrete tasks, while semantic retrieval helped with ambiguous requirements. The findings highlight trade-offs in accuracy, token use, and tool design, underscoring the need to match retrieval tools to task types. By Le

title: How LinkedIn, Netflix & DoorDash Run Agents, Evals & Inference in Production: QCon AI New York 2026
summary: QCon AI New York has published its full program for December 15–16, 2026. Engineers from LinkedIn, Netflix, DoorDash, Figma, Pinterest, Honeycomb, Harvey, Google DeepMind and OpenAI describe AI systems they run in production. Talks cover agent permissions and guardrails, eval loops, inference cost, AI code review, and team adoption. By Artenisa Chatziou

title: Presentation: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry

By J

title: Article: The iOS Crash We Could Not Reproduce
summary: This article describes the investigation to find the root cause of a production crash in a large-scale iOS consumer app that had no clean stack trace. The crash occurred intermittently and resisted every local reproduction attempt. The final code change was small, but identifying the root cause required turning a vague SIGBUS report into a controlled set of experiments. By Abhishek Gang Deb

title: Angular's TypeScript 7-Powered Compiler Enters Beta with Rust-Based Preprocessor
summary: The Angular team has introduced ngp, a compiler preprocessor that rewrites the analysis stage in Rust using Oxc. It replaces ngc's dependence on the Transformer API, which TypeScript 7.0 removed. An early benchmark showed 2x to 3x faster cold builds. Adoption is expected in an Angular 22 minor release; production builds should stay on ngc until then. By Daniel Curtis

title: Cloudflare Makes Basin Serverless Analytics Generally Available
summary: Cloudflare has announced the general availability of Basin, a serverless analytics platform built on Apache Iceberg and R2 Object Storage. The managed service supports open data formats and integrates with tools such as DuckDB, Snowflake, and Apache Spark, with no data egress fees. By Renato Losio

title: Google Finds That Technical Debt Can Derail Coding Agents through "Agent Distraction"
summary: In a recent article, Google senior staff software engineer Sam Saccone and senior staff data scientist Madhuri Garikapati highlighted the cost of agent distraction, where AI coding agents get derailed by stale technical debt, such as old TODO comments, obsolete bug references, and outdated specs, leading them to embark on unrequested "side-quests".
